text:
maya: FYI — just noticed a customer saw odd quota behavior during short spikes. requests go through for a few seconds, then we start dropping and their key accumulates "debt" that doesn't reconcile quickly.

jonathan: which scope? per-key or org-wide?

maya: per-key. trace shows token bucket allowed a big burst, server accepted, then later we enforce by clamping and sending 429s. but the credit "debt" number keeps growing and client had to wait ~minutes. expected it to amortize faster. :thinking:

liam: that's the classic reconcile window vs. accounting mismatch. are we deducting at admit time or completion time?

maya: admit time. we subtract tokens when request starts. problem is we also have a short-grace window that lets us overdraw a bit, but reconciliation only happens on a slow background task every 60s.

jonathan: can we shorten reconcile for short-burst keys? eg. amortize negative balance linearly over 10s for debts under a threshold.

anita: dashboard telemetry needs to show that — we currently only show 1m and 5m burn rates. ops couldn't tell it was a 6s spike vs sustained load. we should add a short-window metric (5s/10s) and a per-key debt histogram.

kai: client-side guidance would also help. we can emit clearer signals so SDKs back off earlier. Two ideas: return 429 + Retry-After when debt exceeds limit, or include a header like `X-Burst-Credit-Remaining` so smart clients can throttle before a hard 429.

liam: I prefer headers for graceful client behaviour. 429 should be reserved for when we need to shed load. header example: 

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Burst-Credit-Remaining: -120
X-Burst-Credit-RecoverSecs: 8
```

Then SDKs can apply soft backoff if remaining < 0. If extreme, server returns 429: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 3
```

jonathan: careful: exposing internal credit numbers may let clients game the system, but SDKs from Redwood are trusted for now. public customers might not want that telemetry surfaced. could gate it by tier.

anita: agreed, maybe a console toggle per-customer to enable verbose headers for debug. default off. also need dashboard signals: `burst.credit.debt`, `burst.recover_seconds`, plus alert rule when avg debt > X for >30s.

kai: on the algorithm side: propose two-tier reconcile: immediate micro-amortize pass for debts within +/- max_grace (5–10s window) that runs every 1s, and periodic reclaim pass for larger debts every 60s. that minimizes perceived latency for short spikes.

liam: micro-pass sounds good but watch CPU cost. doing it every 1s for all keys is expensive. do it only for keys that recently overdrew (track hot set).

maya: current implementation already tracks recent overdraft keys in a hot cache. we can trigger micro-pass for keys in that set. cost should be modest.

jonathan: how do we handle rollouts? we don't want to flip behavior globally and break clients that assume old semantics.

maya: plan: implement feature flag behind console toggle + default behavior change for canary orgs. rollout steps: 1) internal canary, 2) 5% external, 3) ramp to 50% with telemetry gating, 4) full. also surface a "burst-mode" field in /v1/usage or /v1/describe so SDKs know which behavior they're seeing.

anita: add UX in console: show per-key short-window spike chart + a reconciliation timeline (events when debt was amortized). Product will want a tooltip explaining what debt means.

liam: what about mitigation for abusive clients that piggyback on grace? need a hard cap: negative_balance_limit = max_burst * 2. once exceeded -> immediate 429 + ban window.

kai: and add backoff guidance for SDKs: expo backoff with full jitter starting at 50ms up to 5s, but if Retry-After header set, respect it. also show a client example in SDK docs.

maya: I'll draft an RFC with: algorithm pseudocode, header semantics, telemetry names, rollout plan, and console UX mock.

jonathan: please include an opt-in header policy for enterprise customers to expose verbose headers. legal/security should review.

anita: I'll mock dashboard panels and an alert rule. want to include a sample query for the metrics team.

liam: sample pseudocode for micro-amortize: 

```
if key in hot_overdraw_set:
  delta = min(abs(debt), floor(max_burst/5))
  debt += delta   # amortize towards 0
  emit(metric: burst.credit.debt)
```

kai: looks fine. remember to account for concurrency (multiple routers). reconcile should be eventually consistent but safe. use CAS on credit shard.

maya: sre-bot created INC-2026-142 for the initial customer report. attaching traces in the RFC.

sre-bot: [incident] INC-2026-142 created by maya — link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-142

maya: timeline: I'll put a draft RFC up by EOD, want reviewers: jonathan, liam, anita, kai. prefer to land server-side headers + micro-pass behind flag first, then SDK doc update.

jonathan: +1. thanks for catching this.

liam: one more ask — include a regression test that simulates 1–10s spikes and ensures debt amortizes within 15s for small spikes.

maya: will add tests.

anita: I'll add dashboard panels to the canary checklist. :white_check_mark:

kai: SDK patch drafted once headers are stable.

maya: great — moving to RFC now.
